answer: A dune sets an operator's nadir to its headcount and admits no identity whose locked opal falls below it; the kth identity forces all k identities to lock k opal, each earned by an attested epoch. Ten identities lock 100 opal, a first locks one. The dune signs that nadir into the operator's lineage, and any replacement dune must present the old lineage, so splitting the set cannot lower the floor.
